saints.name: Sts. Cosmas and Damian
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Twin physicians who healed the sick without payment for the love of Christ, and were crowned with martyrdom…
biography: Cosmas and Damian, held by tradition to be twin brothers born in Arabia, practised medicine at the seaport of Aegeae in Cilicia and would accept no fee for their care, observing the Lord's word, 'Freely you have received, freely give.' For this the Greeks named them the Anargyroi, the moneyless ones, and their charity won many to the faith.

In the persecution under Diocletian they were arrested by order of Lysias, governor of Cilicia, and, refusing to renounce Christ, were beheaded with their brothers Anthimus, Leontius, and Euprepius, about the year 287. Their relics were buried at Cyrrhus in Syria, which became a shrine that the Emperor Justinian adorned in thanksgiving for a cure ascribed to their prayers.

About 530 Pope Felix IV dedicated a basilica to them in the Roman Forum, famed for its sixth-century mosaics, and their names are still invoked together in the Roman Canon of the Mass. As physicians who healed without payment, they are the patrons of physicians, surgeons, and pharmacists.
saints.knownFor: Healing the sick without charge and their martyrdom for the faith.
